scenarios.title: Sharing Toys
scenarios.teach: Sharing means letting others use or enjoy things together with you.
scenarios.prompt: You're playing with your favorite toy. Your friend asks if they can play too. What do you do?

choices.text: Say no and keep playing alone
choices.feedback: That might make your friend feel left out.

choices.text: Take turns playing with the toy
choices.feedback: Great choice! Sharing makes everyone happy.

scenarios.discussion: Talk about a time you shared something with a friend. How did it feel?

scenarios.title: Saying Sorry
scenarios.teach: Apologizing means admitting a mistake and showing you care about how someone else feels.
scenarios.prompt: You accidentally knock over your friend's block tower. What should you do?

choices.text: Walk away and say nothing
choices.feedback: It's kind to own up to mistakes.

choices.text: Say sorry and help rebuild it
choices.feedback: Nice! Apologizing and helping fix things shows real care.

scenarios.discussion: Why is it important to say sorry even when we didn't mean to make a mistake?

scenarios.title: Waiting Your Turn
scenarios.teach: Waiting your turn means being patient and fair to the people around you.
scenarios.prompt: You really want to go down the slide, but two kids are ahead of you in line. What do you do?

choices.text: Cut in front of them
choices.feedback: Cutting in line isn't fair to others waiting.

choices.text: Wait patiently for your turn
choices.feedback: Awesome! Waiting your turn is fair to everyone.

scenarios.discussion: How do you feel when someone cuts in front of you? How can we remember to be patient?

scenarios.title: Being a Good Listener
scenarios.teach: Listening means paying full attention when someone else is speaking.
scenarios.prompt: Your teacher is giving instructions, but you want to talk to your friend. What should you do?

choices.text: Keep talking to your friend
choices.feedback: It's easy to miss important instructions this way.

choices.text: Listen quietly to the teacher
choices.feedback: Great! Good listening helps you learn and shows respect.

scenarios.discussion: Why does it help others when we listen quietly while they're speaking?

scenarios.title: Helping a Friend
scenarios.teach: Helping others is a kind thing to do whenever someone needs a hand.
scenarios.prompt: You see a friend trip and drop their books. What do you do?

choices.text: Walk past without helping
choices.feedback: A little help can make someone's day better.

choices.text: Stop and help pick up the books
choices.feedback: Wonderful! Helping others is a great way to show kindness.

scenarios.discussion: Can you think of another time you could help a friend or family member?

scenarios.title: Telling the Truth
scenarios.teach: Honesty means always telling the truth, even when it feels hard.
scenarios.prompt: You broke a vase by accident. Your parent asks what happened. What do you do?

choices.text: Say you don't know what happened
choices.feedback: Being honest, even about mistakes, builds trust.

choices.text: Tell the truth about what happened
choices.feedback: Great! Being honest is always the best choice, even when it's hard.

scenarios.discussion: Why is it important to tell the truth even when we're scared we'll get in trouble?

scenarios.title: Respecting Personal Space
scenarios.teach: Personal space means giving others room and asking before touching their things or bodies.
scenarios.prompt: Your friend doesn't want a hug right now. What should you do?

choices.text: Hug them anyway
choices.feedback: It's important to respect when someone says no.

choices.text: Respect their choice and don't hug them
choices.feedback: Great! Respecting personal space shows you care about their feelings.

scenarios.discussion: Why is it important to ask before hugging or touching someone?

scenarios.title: Disagreeing Respectfully
scenarios.teach: Sometimes we disagree with friends, and that's okay if we talk about it calmly.
scenarios.prompt: You and your friend want to play different games. What's a good way to solve this?

choices.text: Yell until they agree with you
choices.feedback: Yelling doesn't help solve disagreements.

choices.text: Talk calmly and find a game you both enjoy
choices.feedback: Great! Talking calmly helps solve disagreements fairly.

scenarios.discussion: What's a fair way to decide what to do when friends want different things?

scenarios.title: Following Directions
scenarios.teach: Rules and directions help keep everyone safe and things running smoothly.
scenarios.prompt: Your teacher asks everyone to line up quietly, but your friends are talking loudly. What do you do?

choices.text: Join in and talk loudly too
choices.feedback: Following directions helps keep the classroom calm and safe.

choices.text: Follow the teacher's directions and stay quiet
choices.feedback: Great! Following directions shows respect and helps everyone.

scenarios.discussion: Why do rules and directions help keep us safe?

scenarios.title: Saying Thank You
scenarios.teach: Gratitude means noticing and appreciating the kind things people do for us.
scenarios.prompt: Your grandma gives you a gift you didn't expect. What should you say?

choices.text: Nothing, just take the gift
choices.feedback: Saying thank you shows you appreciate their kindness.

choices.text: Say thank you and smile
choices.feedback: Wonderful! Showing gratitude makes people feel appreciated.

scenarios.discussion: Can you think of someone you could thank today?
